name: RotaCentral
shortDescription: UK volunteer rota software for places of worship and other voluntary organisations, with allocation or self-sign-up, availability, swaps and email or SMS reminders.
suitableContexts: Churches that need either leader allocation or volunteer self-sign-up
Teams that need availability, confirmation and reminder workflows

gdprInformation: RotaCentral Limited publishes a privacy notice identifying itself as processor for customer organisations. It states that its application uses a UK Amazon data centre, that rota attendance and contact records are retained for seven years after the relevant shift or most recent shift, and that it does not transfer data outside the UK. Request the current agreement, full sub-processor list, security evidence, deletion process and export format before adoption.
coreFeatures: Dashboard for gaps and attention items
support: Supplier offers a demo request route
Supplier offers a free trial route
Website describes premium support but does not publish a support-hours commitment on the reviewed pages

uk-operator.value: The supplier's privacy notice identifies RotaCentral Limited as a company registered in England and Wales. Companies House records RotaCentral Limited (10417157) as active.

worship-relevance.value: The supplier lists places of worship among the organisations using its volunteer rota software.

pricing.value: Supplier publishes annual GBP tiers from £135 to £360, plus an Enterprise enquiry option and a free trial route.

data-handling.value: Supplier's privacy notice describes processor status, UK application hosting, no stated overseas transfers and seven-year retention of rota attendance and contact records.

editorial.assessment: RotaCentral is a general UK volunteer-scheduling service rather than a church-management system, but its published place-of-worship relevance and roster workflows make it a credible specialist option for churches. Its public privacy notice is unusually useful for an initial comparison: it identifies the processor role, a stated UK hosting location and named retention periods. A church should still test ministry-specific rota needs and obtain the current contractual and security material before importing personal data.
bestFor: Churches that need a focused rota system rather than a wider member database
Teams needing a mix of self-sign-up and administrator allocation
Churches that value published annual GBP prices and explicit public retention information
strengths: UK company and published UK-facing privacy notice
Places of worship are an explicit supplier use case
Allocation, self-sign-up, availability, swaps and confirmation are published workflows
Published annual GBP tiers cover small through large volunteer groups
Privacy notice states UK application hosting and retention periods
limitations: It is a general volunteer platform rather than church-specific software
Published pages do not establish church member-management, giving, safeguarding or service-planning features
No published import, export, accessibility or full sub-processor detail was found in the reviewed material
SMS delivery arrangements and associated data handling should be confirmed in writing

procurementVerdict.problem: Creating and confirming recurring church volunteer rotas without spreadsheet and messaging overhead
procurementVerdict.differentiator: A UK-operated, focused rota service that supports both allocated and self-selected shifts and publishes useful initial data-handling detail
procurementVerdict.firstCheck: Run one real ministry rota through availability, role matching, self-sign-up, allocation, reminders, swaps, absence and export requirements before moving the full team
